container.env.prompt.content:
I am using the container development environment of "WARMY". Please help me set up the development environment on this machine / inside this container.

[Context]
- This is a **container**-based development environment; I am using whichever runtime you selected (Docker / Podman / WSL / …, whichever we are actually using).
- The project directory is mounted inside the container at: /workspace (that is our convention; if the real mount point differs, trust what you see in `pwd` / `mount`).
- I do **not** know which distribution this container runs — do not install anything based on a guess.

[Step 1: probe first, then act]
Please run and show the output of: `cat /etc/os-release`, `uname -m`, `which node python3 java go`, and whichever of `apt --version` / `apk --version` / `dnf --version` / `yum --version` exists;
then **pick the package manager based on the real distribution you detected** (Debian/Ubuntu -> apt; Alpine -> apk; Fedora/RHEL -> dnf/yum). Do **not** assume a package manager before probing.

[Step 2: explain and verify]
For everything you install, state what it is, its version, where it went (path), how to verify it really works (give the verification command), and **write the whole procedure down** so I can replay it when rebuilding the environment.

[Step 3: persistence (important)]
Software installed in the container writable layer **survives stopping/starting the same container, but is lost once the container is deleted and recreated**. So also give me three things: (1) avoid recreating this container; (2) turn the steps into a Dockerfile / script for rebuilds; (3) use "solidify current environment" (snapshot/commit) to freeze the installed environment.

[Network]
If installing is slow or failing, tell me how to switch to a faster/mirror package source (apt / pip / npm) and which files that changes.

[⛔ Security requirement]
**Never write keys / tokens / passwords into files inside the container**: snapshot/commit freezes the entire filesystem at that moment, so secrets would be baked into the image. Inject credentials via environment variables, and never persist them.

container.env.solidify.decision.before-d: Before a container may be destroyed ⇒ always solidify once (last chance)

container.env.solidify.decision.throttle: Changed and past the throttle window ⇒ solidify once
container.env.solidify.executorHost: Architecture: the **AI executor stays on the host**; only the *user project's* commands/tools go into the container — so nothing needs Node in the image on our executor's behalf.
container.env.solidify.keep: Only the latest {n} solidify artifacts are kept (manually cleanable), otherwise the disk fills up.
container.env.solidify.refused.coalesced: A solidify already happened within the throttle window, so this one is skipped (one image per keystroke would be worse).
container.env.solidify.refused.commit-fa: Solidify failed (commit did not succeed): the raw output is in the diagnostic event stream, and **no** "solidified" record was written.
container.env.solidify.refused.commit-un: commit reported success but the image could not be read back, so this counts as a failure (we do not pretend it solidified).
container.env.solidify.refused.no-contai: There is no project container to solidify yet: start the project first (starting it creates the project container).
container.env.solidify.refused.no-image: Solidify did not succeed: commit did not actually succeed (no project container, engine unavailable, or the output is in the diagnostic stream) - we never write a fake "solidified" record.
container.env.solidify.refused.no-runtim: No container chosen yet: pick one from the project right-click menu first.
container.env.solidify.refused.nothing-t: There is nothing to solidify right now, so nothing is executed.
container.env.solidify.refused.runtime-c: This runtime cannot be solidified programmatically by us — follow the ability note above and do it manually.
container.env.solidify.restore: Rolling back to a solidify point belongs to the **environment** dimension and is separate from file rollback points.
container.env.solidify.retained: The project container is **kept by default** (long-lived, no --rm) ⇒ stopping/starting keeps the writable layer; that alone already gives "the next start returns to the previous state".
container.env.solidify.security: ⛔ Security notice: commit freezes the **entire filesystem at that moment** (**including potential keys / caches / temp files**). Never write secrets into container files; we **never** delete your files on our own.
container.env.solidify.throttle: Solidifying is **not "on every change"**: `docker diff` only shows how many files changed and cannot tell an installed package from cache/logs ⇒ we **throttle** (at most once per {s}s) and solidify at explicit moments (your button / before a container may be destroyed).
container.env.solidify.title: Solidify the environment (freeze it into a layer)
container.env.solidify.why.isolation-lev: It is only an isolation level, not a standalone engine
container.env.solidify.why.no-runtime-ch: No container chosen yet, so the solidify ability cannot be determined
container.env.solidify.why.oci-commit: OCI engines (Docker / Podman …) can freeze the current state into a layer
container.env.solidify.why.one-shot-vm: A one-shot sandbox VM has no persistent environment to solidify
container.env.solidify.why.runtime-unkno: The solidify ability of this runtime is unknown (stated honestly, no fake support)
container.env.solidify.why.system-servic: System containers are managed by a system service; solidifying needs elevation, which we do not run for you
container.env.solidify.why.wsl-no-commit: **WSL has no commit**: only `wsl --export/--import` of the whole disk (large and slow), which we do not run for you
container.envType.android.why: **Not a container**: docker-android style images simply run an Android emulator inside a Linux container (needs KVM; inside WSL2 it also needs nested virtualization and is finicky), or you use an emulator directly (Android SDK AVD / Genymotion / Waydroid). This app does **not** build its own Android emulator; it only explains and points you elsewhere.

container.snapshot.body: **Under bind mounts a container snapshot does not cover project files**: commit snapshots the **container writable layer**, while the project directory is mounted from the host and lies outside it — so "a container makes project rollback easier" is **not true**. **File rollback = existing checkpoint mechanism** (git / shadow-git / CoW): **independent of container**; checkpoints are required even without a container. **Environment rollback = container image / snapshot**: rollback points can be upgraded to "files + environment fingerprint" (image digest / env revision). We will **not** claim that a container rollback point is simpler; rollback is layered: files still depend on us, environment on snapshots.
container.snapshot.fingerprint: Bonus: **rollback points are upgraded to "files + environment fingerprint"** — each point also records the image digest / environment revision of that moment, so "code rolled back but environment changed" is flagged in advance.
container.snapshot.layerFiles: File rollback = existing checkpoint mechanism (independent of container)

llm.appendWrongPlace: [Not written] {q} does not exist yet, while the same-name file written earlier in this task is at {p} (currently {n} characters). This part belongs at the end of that file: send it again with write_file on {p} and append:true (copy the path exactly).
llm.archivedCoverage: [This injection covers archives {a}–{b} of {n} in total]
llm.askEchoBlocked: [ask_user] No card shown: "{q}" is a question the user asked you in the task. Answer it directly in your reply instead of asking it back to the user. Use what you already know (the attachment/screenshot content, tool results) to answer it.
llm.chatOnlyPart: (System) Tools are unavailable this turn. Complete only the chat part: answer the user and write what is asked. Do not pretend to do the rest, and do not repeat this note.
llm.completionCheckCut: (Note: the previous round was cut off by the tool-round/budget limit; you did not finish it yourself.)
llm.continueLongTextReply: [Keep writing · not long enough yet] The user asked for {n} characters; so far your replies contain about {x} (the real count measured by the host). Continue **directly in your reply from where the text broke off** — do not repeat what you have already written and do not rewrite the opening — until the length requirement is met.
llm.continueNoAction: [CONTINUE] Your last message only *said* what you would do — you did not call any tool. Call the tool NOW and actually do it, then report briefly. Do not stop after saying "next I will...".
llm.delegateUseIt: (These sub-tasks have **already been completed for you by this machine's specialist models**: answer the user **using those results directly**. Do not say "I cannot see images / cannot read audio / I lack that capability" — that is factually wrong, the capability was filled in by the sub-task. If the results are not enough, say what is missing.)
llm.dutySystem: You are the duty agent of a WArmy project group. Reply briefly; you may use board commands.
llm.etaAnomaly: ⚠️ [Stopped · treated as an anomaly] The same task has exceeded the model's own completion estimate {n} times in a row (last estimate: {eta} left, but it ran {over} more). Check progress before deciding to continue.
llm.identityAnchor: [IDENTITY ANCHOR · restated every turn] You are "{ming}", the user's AI workhorse; the user is the person you serve. This never changes — no matter how long the context, which model engine is swapped in midway, or how many auto-continued rounds happen. Do NOT claim to be qwen / any base model, and do NOT mention training provenance. You only ever recognize one relationship: you are the workhorse, they are the person you serve.
llm.identityAnon: You are an AI workhorse in WArmy.
llm.imagesFromTaskStart: (These images were attached by the user at the start of this task: {names}. They are not a new task; use them only to answer the task's questions about images/attachments.)
llm.imagesVisible: Images attached this turn are already visible to you; do not read_file them. If unclear, say so honestly.
llm.ledgerHead: [What I have already done in this task (host execution log: all succeeded, results are in effect, not to be redone)]
llm.ledgerTail: Next I only do the parts that are not done yet; if any of the above is called again, the host just returns the original result and does not run it again.
llm.ledgerTruncated: … (the execution log was too long, truncated to {n} characters; earlier actions are still in the session ledger — ask by index if you need them)
llm.lengthProgress: [Length progress] The user asked for {n} characters: {p} now has {y} characters (counted without whitespace or line breaks; {x} including them), about {z} to go ⇒ next, call write_file on the same path with append:true to write the next part (800–1500 characters per part). The host reports the count after every write, so do not count it yourself (no reading the file back, scripts or commands to count).
llm.lengthProgressDone: [Length progress] The user asked for {n} characters: {p} now has {y} characters (counted without whitespace or line breaks; {x} including them), which meets the requirement — do not write more into it and do not count again; go straight to the other parts that are not finished yet.
llm.lengthProgressSoft: [Length progress] The user asked for {n} characters: {p} now has {y} characters (counted without whitespace or line breaks; {x} including them). · If **this file** is the {n}-character piece the user asked for: call write_file on the same path with append:true for the next part (800–1500 characters per part) — the host reports the count after every write. · If this is just another, shorter deliverable and the long piece has **not been started**: ignore this line and create that long file directly (the host will report the count on it). Never count characters yourself by reading the file, writing a script or running a command.
llm.lengthStall: [Length progress] {p} now has {y} characters (the user asked for about {n}). **Three consecutive writes each added fewer than {k} characters ⇒ the host judges this stretch can no longer be written and stops urging you to continue**: stop writing to this file, report the real progress and the character count ({y}) to the user exactly as it is, and let the user decide whether to continue.
llm.longForm: The user wants long-form writing: produce it completely. Do not stop early, do not omit, do not give only an outline or an opening; aim for the requested length (e.g. “N words”) and write until a natural end.
llm.modelLine: You run on the model engine "{model}" — the engine is only the tool that carries you, **not your identity**. If asked "which model are you", you may state the engine; **if asked "who are you", answer that you are "{ming}", the workhorse**. Never claim to be qwen / any base model name, and never mention training provenance.
llm.needText: Answer the user directly in short text. Do not call tools.
llm.needTextPlain: (System) The machine has already performed the needed operations. Reply to the user in plain text with the conclusion/result; do not narrate internal steps or repeat this note.
llm.openWrongPlace: [open_path] File not found: {q}. The same-name file produced in this task is at {p} — if that is what the user should see, call open_path on that path (copy it exactly).
llm.planContinue: [CONTINUE PLAN] Proceed with the next step (actually do the work with tools — do not just say you will). When done, mark it verified with plan_verify, then continue.
llm.planContinueFail: (Auto-continue of the next step failed; stopped.)
llm.planFirst: [MULTI-STEP TASK] If this needs three or more things, or several steps in order, first list them with plan_update (id / title / status), then do each one and mark it verified with plan_verify; the Plan card on the right shows progress live.
llm.planGate: [Plan gate] Only when what the user asks for this time involves 3 or more distinct steps (e.g. create a file + open it + wait + write a long text) should you first call plan_update to list a plan and then complete it step by step; for a single step, a plain question or small talk, do not create a plan — just do it. Write each step as one verifiable action (start with a verb, do not copy the user's wording, never turn an attachment name or a path into a step), at most 10 steps; only 1 step may be doing at a time; mark a step done as soon as it is finished, and attach evidence with plan_verify when needed. If a plan already exists, only update the statuses — do not rebuild it.
llm.planStop: (The plan still has unfinished steps, but this round's auto-continue limit is reached. Tell me to continue if needed.)
llm.planVerifyOnly: [Continue plan · verify only] Step {id} "{title}" you already reported as done, but there is no evidence yet. Do **not redo it** (do not rewrite the same file or reopen the same thing). Do exactly two things: 1) verify the ground truth at minimal cost (e.g. read_file / dir / check the file exists and its size); 2) mark it with plan_verify including the real evidence, then continue with the next step.
llm.productLine: This is the desktop app WArmy. You may write files and use tools; if you cannot do something, say so honestly.
llm.recentUserTasks: [What the user asked for in this session] When you need to "continue / redo the task above", go by these (do not say you cannot see them):
llm.recentUserTasksCont: [What the user asked for in this session] (verbatim, for reference only) This round is a continuation: **do not redo the parts that are already done** (go by the execution log and the last instruction); only do what is not finished yet:
llm.stallEtaOk: (Warning threshold reached; the model judged it is NOT stalled and expects {eta} more to finish. Threshold raised.)
llm.stallEtaOver: (The model's own completion estimate has been exceeded {n} time(s); continuing with its new estimate: {eta} left.)
llm.stallOk: (Warning threshold reached; the model judged it is NOT stalled, so execution continues and the threshold was raised.)
llm.stallWarn: ⚠️ [Likely stalled — stopped] Auto-run hit a warning threshold ({why}). The analysis model concluded: {reason}. The task may be stuck or looping; please review before continuing.
llm.stepAppendDone: this exact chunk has already been appended
llm.stepGenExists: this file was already generated in this task (to really regenerate it with new content, pass overwrite:true)
llm.stepGenSame: a document with the same content has already been generated
llm.stepOpenDone: [Done · not redone] {p} was already opened in this task; the host did not open it again (the user already sees it). Go straight to what is not done yet; once everything is done, report in text.
llm.stepSameNameElsewhere: this task already produced a file with the same name at {p}; this {q} would make another copy in a different place (to change that file, use edit_file on {p} or rewrite it with overwrite:true; only if the user really wants a second copy in the new place, send again with overwrite:true)
llm.stepWaitDone: the wait the user asked for has already been completed in this task ({n} time(s))
llm.stepWriteElsewhere: the same content has already been written to another file
llm.stepWriteSame: this file has already been written with exactly the same content
llm.strictLanguage: [LANGUAGE RULE] Always answer in {lang}: both your thinking and your reply must be in {lang}, with no other languages mixed in.
llm.timeLine: The current time is {time} (timezone {tz}, epoch {epoch}). Call get_time when you need an exact instant or network time; for "wait N seconds" compute from the epoch, do not guess.
llm.toolLimitParam: Number of cards to return (1-20, default 5)
llm.toolMaxCharsParam: Max characters returned per call (default 4000, cap 8000)
llm.toolOffsetParam: Start character offset (default 0; use it to page through long records)
llm.toolQueryParam: Search string: keywords or the user question as-is.
llm.toolRecallDesc: Search the elided conversation history by meaning/keywords. When the view shows an elision pointer ("[已省略 N 条历史 ...]") and you need a detail from it (who said what, a conclusion, a number, a path), you MUST call this instead of guessing. Args: query (string), optional limit (1-20, default 5). Returns up to `limit` cards with seq, recordId, snippet and hit source; then call retrieve on any of them for the byte-exact original.
llm.toolRecordIdParam: Record id (recordId="m-..." as shown in the pointer)
llm.toolRetrieveDesc: Fetch the byte-exact original of elided log entries by seq or recordId. Prefer the seq range and recordId samples given in the pointer. Args: recordId (string) OR seq (integer), optional offset (start char, default 0) and maxChars (per-call cap, default 4000). Returns the raw text; if it was truncated the result states the total length and the next offset so you can page through the whole record.
llm.toolSeqParam: Log sequence number (any integer inside the pointer seq range)
llm.userAnon: Your user is the local operator; call them you and do not invent a name.
llm.userCallRule: When addressing the user, use only the name "{u}"; do not use "boss", "master", "user" or other generic titles (unless that is their actual name).
llm.userLine: Your user is "{u}"; address them by this name.

llm.writeOverwriteBody: This will replace a file written in this task with shorter content: {old} → {new} characters. Overwriting loses the original; appending puts this content after it.

model.ctxBudgetHint: How much context window this workhorse may use for its workers. Defaults to 60%, with a 32K-token floor (if the window is smaller, it uses the whole window).
model.deleteConfirm: Remove this model from the chain? This cannot be undone.
model.editProviderConfirmBody: This will close the dialog and open Settings → Models to edit the provider. Any models you selected here will be discarded. Continue?
model.fenLeiHint: Model chain for decision/routing (RLCD-style: small and fast, confidence-scored judgments) — intent classification, message routing, judge/approval. Prefer a dedicated decision model (e.g. Jev); a small chat model can substitute. First enabled = default; move up/down or disable.
model.fetchHint: Click Fetch to load the provider model list
model.fillRequired: Please enter a model name, and select at least one input type, output type, and capability
model.kindHint.asr: **ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition)**: speech to text. Voice input and audio transcription use this chain.
model.kindHint.chat: **LLM / MoE (Large Language Model / Mixture of Experts)**: the main model for chat, writing, reasoning. Also acts as the global chat whitelist.
model.kindHint.code: **Code LLM**: specialist for writing, editing, reviewing and refactoring code.
model.kindHint.embed: **Embedding**: turns text into vectors for memory retrieval and similarity.
model.kindHint.fenLei: **Classifier / LRM (decision)**: automatic classification, judging, routing (intent, moderation, JEV-style decision models). Falls back to the chat chain when none is available.
model.kindHint.imageUnd: **VLM (Vision-Language Model)**: understands images (recognition, reading text in images, screenshots). Opposite of the image generation model.
model.kindHint.ocr: **OCR (Optical Character Recognition)**: extracts text and layout from images/scans.
model.kindHint.organizer: **SLM (Small Language Model)**: lightweight summarization/organizing — a small cheap model is enough.
model.kindHint.reasoning: **LRM (Large Reasoning Model)**: complex multi-step reasoning and self-verification. Hand over hard reasoning when the current model cannot.
model.kindHint.rerank: **Reranker**: reorders retrieval results to improve recall accuracy.
model.kindHint.safety: **Guardrail**: input/output compliance checking. Falls back to the chat model if absent.
model.kindHint.translate: **MT (Machine Translation)**: dedicated translation, usually better than a general chat model.
model.kindHint.videoUnd: **Video-LMM**: understands video content (scene understanding, key points).

model.smartHint: Checked: the system arranges the chain for you. Unchecked: order/disable models yourself.

net.banner.dismissHint: Dismissing hides this reason; it appears again when the state changes.

net.dialability.ipv6Natural: This machine has a global IPv6 address (naturally dialable)
net.domainTitle: Public address list (IPs and/or domains; multiple allowed)
net.emptyList: Add at least one public address (IP or domain) first
net.helpBody: Mesh links multiple WArmy machines into a private network so remote agents can join local groups/projects. Usually at least one machine needs a publicly dialable address; if both sides sit behind NAT and cannot connect directly, configure a relay. When mesh is off, local address facts (IPv6 / dialability) remain visible, but remote sessions cannot be established.
net.hint: Mesh links multiple WARMY machines into a private network.
net.host.autoAdded: The detected public IP was added to the host addresses automatically.
net.host.autoDuplicate: The detected public IP is already in the host address list; it was not added again.
net.host.autoFull: The host address list already has 10 entries, so the detected public IP was not added automatically; remove one first.
net.host.defaultPortHint: When the port is omitted, 59599 is displayed and used; IPv6 requires brackets when a port is included.
net.host.detectTimeout: Detection timed out: no local/public address was obtained, so direct reachability cannot be concluded.
net.host.duplicate: This address is already in the list (duplicates are judged by the normalized host:port).
net.host.empty: No host addresses yet. Add one manually, or use the detect button above to fill in the public IP automatically.
net.host.enableNote: Note: this checkbox only records the intent “others may reach me at these addresses”. This version has not wired host mode into the protocol layer, so it does not mean the port is listening or that others can actually connect.
net.host.errHost: Invalid address: enter an IP, a domain or host:port; for IPv6 use [::1]:59599.
net.host.errIpv6: Invalid IPv6 address (when a port is included it must be written as [::1]:59599).
net.host.errPort: The port must be an integer from 1 to 65535.
net.host.full: Host addresses are limited to 10; remove one before adding another.
net.host.hint: Host mode = the addresses others can use to reach you. Each entry may be an IP, a domain, or host:port; when the port is omitted, 59599 is used. For IPv6 write [::1]:59599.
net.host.isPublicNo: No (this host is behind a private network / NAT)
net.host.noPublic: No public IP was detected (there may be no public egress).
net.host.parserMissing: The address parser did not load, so entries cannot be added right now (restart the app).
net.host.reachDirectUnverified: Directly reachable (inbound connectivity not yet verified)
net.host.removeConfirm: Remove {host} from the host address list?
net.invalidIp: Invalid address (an IP or a domain name is required)
net.invalidPort: Port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
net.ladder.needsConfig: Implemented, not wired in (needs explicit port-mapping consent / STUN servers configured)
net.ladder.none: Not connected (no live session and no rung selected)

net.note.wanManual: Across the public internet without a server: add the peer's public IP:port under Add node; one side needs a port mapping or a publicly reachable host.
net.portBindFailedBody: Port {port} cannot be bound ({error}), so the mesh did not start. Your configured port was NOT changed automatically: pick an available port below, or type one yourself and retry.
net.portConventionHint: The port can be changed to any value from 1 to 65535 at any time. Conventions only, not restrictions: development typically uses {dev} and testing typically uses {test}.
net.portSuggestChecking: Bind-testing available ports on this machine…
net.portSuggestHint: Suggestions only: clicking one just fills the port field (not a whitelist — you can always type any port).
net.portSuggestMeasured: These ports were actually bind-tested on this machine ({probed} tested; only usable ones are listed):
net.portSuggestNone: No usable port was found this time (they may all be taken). You can type any port from 1 to 65535 and retry.
net.provider.addressHint: Write the address as host:port; when the port is omitted, 59599 is used. For IPv6 use [::1]:59599. Addresses must be unique.
net.provider.credPendingNote: The credential was not persisted or written to settings; this entry is marked “pending secure storage” and you can edit it later to retry.
net.provider.credentialKeep: Leave blank to keep the existing credential; a new value overwrites the old one in SecureKeyStore.
net.provider.credentialPlaceholder: Sent only to SecureKeyStore; never written to the settings file.
net.provider.deleteConfirm: Delete hosting provider “{name}”? Only this metadata is removed; there is currently no UI entry to delete the encrypted credential from SecureKeyStore.
net.provider.duplicate: This address is already used by another provider.
net.provider.hint: Register providers that offer host access here. Names and addresses are stored; credentials go only to the main process SecureKeyStore and are never echoed in plaintext by the UI.
net.provider.invalidAddress: Invalid address: use host:port (default 59599; for IPv6 use [::1]:59599).
net.provider.invalidName: The name cannot be empty and must be at most 80 characters.
net.provider.name: Name
net.relay.missing.needsPublicRelay: Both ends cannot connect directly — a machine with a public address is needed as a relay
net.relay.missing.noneConfigured: Both ends are behind NAT and cannot connect directly — you need a machine with a public address to act as a relay
net.relay.missing.unreachable: Direct connection is impossible and none of the configured relays are reachable
net.relay.notNeeded.inboundExpected: Waiting for the peer to dial in (this machine is reachable)

net.rung.ipv6Direct: Connected directly over IPv6 (no NAT, no hole-punching needed)

privacy.body:
IN ONE LINE. WArmy is local-first desktop software: there is no server-side account system and no backend of ours that receives your data. Apart from what you voluntarily post to GitHub or send by email, the maintainer holds no personal data about you.

WHERE DATA LIVES. Chats and messages (local JSONL, the source of truth), projects/groups/board, memory indexes (SQLite/vector, rebuildable from the log), knowledge base and archives, audit log, settings and network config live in your local user-data directory by default and are not uploaded automatically. Note: most of these files are NOT encrypted at rest; they rely on your OS account and disk encryption. Only the identity private key, mnemonic, model API keys and social passwords use OS secure storage (Windows DPAPI / macOS Keychain).

WHEN IT GOES ONLINE. Only when you act or configure it: (1) cloud models you configure; (2) local Ollama (default 127.0.0.1, stays on device); (3) update checks (opening About checks automatically; GitHub API and npm registry receive a version query, with no device ID or chat content); (4) skill/plugin market and local speech-model downloads (GitHub / Hugging Face); (5) LAN/public networking (mDNS, direct connections, STUN/port mapping you specify); (6) optional FWArmy relay; (7) WeChat iLink, WeCom, Telegram, Feishu and other IMs you connect; (8) external links you click. We use no analytics, advertising or automatic crash-reporting SDK.

MODELS AND KEYS. You bring your own provider and API key. The key is encrypted locally and sent only as request authentication (usually an Authorization header) to the endpoint you entered, never to the maintainer. Costs, quotas, logging and training are governed by that provider. Content sent to a model may include chats, attachments, tool output and excerpts from memory or knowledge; do not include anything you would not give that provider.

RELAY. FWArmy is an optional, independent, self-hostable relay; the maintainer does not operate it. It forwards end-to-end encrypted envelopes only; queues are in memory with a 30-second TTL and messages are not written to disk. It can still see metadata (DID, IP, time, size, credential usage) and can deny service or substitute public keys. Verify identity fingerprints out of band; use TLS if you expose it publicly.

THIRD-PARTY IM. When you connect WeChat iLink or similar platforms, messages pass through that platform's servers under its privacy policy; the platform may throttle, silently restrict, or change its API. The bot token is encrypted locally; you can disconnect in the app and revoke access on the platform.

LOGS, AUDIT, MEMORY, KNOWLEDGE. The audit log stays local and is never uploaded; you can clear it. It may contain timestamps, session IDs, model IDs, errors and file paths. Memory is an append-only log; the knowledge base contains what you import. Both may be retrieved and sent to a model as context. Deleted chats go to "Recently deleted" and are permanently purged after 48 hours, or you can clear them immediately.

CRASHES AND UPDATES. There is no automatic crash-upload SDK; crash reasons are written to the local warmy-boot.log, and the OS may keep local crash dumps, which we neither upload nor read. If you send us logs, remove usernames, paths and secrets first. Update packages are verified against the SHA-256 from the release feed; this version does not auto-install.

YOUR RIGHTS. You can export chats, an identity backup and a cost CSV; edit or delete local data; and revoke consent in Settings → About (the app quits and asks again next launch). To erase local data, quit the app and delete the user-data directory (Windows: %APPDATA%\@warmy\app-shell; macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/@warmy\app-shell; Linux: ~/.config/@warmy/app-shell or the same name under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME). Uninstalling may not remove it. Delete cloud-model data at the provider; edit or delete GitHub content yourself.

WHAT WE CANNOT DO. There is no server-side account and no "account recovery". The 24-word mnemonic is generated locally and is the only recovery credential; if it is lost, nobody, including the maintainer, can restore it. Compromised devices, malware running as you, third-party plugins or scripts, model providers, IM platforms, and relays you run are outside our control.

CHILDREN / CROSS-BORDER / CHANGES. The software is not directed to children; minors need guardian consent. The maintainer does not transfer data across borders; when you choose a foreign model, IM or relay, you are providing data to it yourself, and you must check local law (e.g. China PIPL cross-border rules, EU GDPR). This policy has a version and effective date; material changes are noted in release notes, and any new off-device transfer will require fresh consent before it is enabled.

TERMS. The Terms of Use also state that AI output may be wrong and needs human review, that the software is provided "as is" without availability guarantees, and that, to the extent permitted by law, the maintainer is not liable for indirect loss. Continued use means you accept them.

CONTACT. Public@numumu.com · Repository and issues: https://github.com/Pondsi/WArmy

QR-code login for personal WeChat is NOT offered (it simulates a client login and risks account bans); personal WeChat only has the iLink ClawBot channel, whose credentials are issued by the provider.
softGate.anthropicAuth: The Anthropic Messages API uses the x-api-key and anthropic-version headers, endpoint /v1/messages; don't reuse the OpenAI Bearer/chat-completions shape.
softGate.assemblyaiAsr: AssemblyAI pre-recorded audio: first /v2/upload, then POST /v2/transcript, then poll /v2/transcript/<id>; put the key directly in the Authorization header, without Bearer.
softGate.deepgramAsr: Deepgram pre-recorded transcription: POST /v1/listen with Authorization: Token <key> and the audio binary as the body; nova-3 + smart_format=true is the recommended default.
softGate.mimoSiteKey: MiMo token-plan keys are not interchangeable between the CN and SGP sites; on 401 first check which site the key belongs to. Prefer streaming for tool calls, and parse reasoning_content and content separately.
softGate.ollamaLocal: Ollama's native root address is usually http://127.0.0.1:11434 without /v1; no API key is needed. If the connection is refused, first make sure the Ollama service and the model are running.
softGate.openaiAuth: OpenAI-compatible APIs usually use Authorization: Bearer <key>; the chat endpoint is /v1/chat/completions. For 401/403 first check that the key matches the site; for 404 first check whether baseURL duplicates or is missing /v1.

net.discovery.hint: Public discoverability publishes your address record to the discovery network so others can find you. Off by default. The record contains only address, port, identity fingerprint, and online time; chat content never enters the discovery layer and messages still go through the server you choose. Once enabled, anyone can read this metadata.
